answer: A cedar-anchored attestation chain resists Sybils by tying each agent's standing to a growing, verifiable work history, not to a self-asserted identity. Every completed task appends a signed receipt, and peers weight new claims by the chain's depth, so a fresh identity starts at the floor and climbs toward its zenith one attested job at a time. Forging a convincing history means doing real work for weeks or buying aged chains, and a ferrous-hard rule caps how fast reputation can rise, so a Sybil farm faces months of effort or a steep price per identity - far more than one fake vote is worth.
